examples.solution_text:
Split the shed into a rectangular prism and a half-cylinder. The roof radius is $10\div2=5\text{ m}$.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{prism}}&=Ah\\&=(10\times4)\times9\\&=360\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{roof}}&=\frac12\pi r^{2}h\\&=\frac12\pi(5)^{2}\times9\\&=112.5\pi\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=V_{\text{prism}}+V_{\text{roof}}\\&=360+112.5\pi\\&\approx713.4\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A cylindrical column stands on a square concrete slab. The slab has side length $7\text{ m}$ and thickness $0.4\text{ m}$. The cylinder has diameter $3\text{ m}$ and height $5\text{ m}$ above the slab. Find the total volume to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
The parts meet at one face, so add their volumes. The cylinder radius is $3\div2=1.5\text{ m}$.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{slab}}&=lwh\\&=7\times7\times0.4\\&=19.6\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{cylinder}}&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi(1.5)^{2}\times5\\&=11.25\pi\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=19.6+11.25\pi\\&\approx54.9\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A cube of edge length $5\text{ cm}$ stands on a cylinder of radius $4\text{ cm}$ and height $7\text{ cm}$. The solids meet without overlapping. Find the total volume to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
Find the volume of each solid, then add.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{cube}}&=l^{3}\\&=5^{3}\\&=125\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{cylinder}}&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi(4)^{2}\times7\\&=112\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=125+112\pi\\&\approx476.9\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A stepped shaft consists of two cylinders sharing the same axis. The lower cylinder has radius $4\text{ cm}$ and height $2\text{ cm}$. The upper cylinder has radius $1.5\text{ cm}$ and height $9\text{ cm}$ above the lower cylinder. Find the total volume to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
The cylinders meet at one face. Calculate each volume separately and add.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{lower}}&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi(4)^{2}\times2\\&=32\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{upper}}&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi(1.5)^{2}\times9\\&=20.25\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=32\pi+20.25\pi\\&=52.25\pi\\&\approx164.1\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

Each hole has radius $4\div2=2\text{ cm}$ and length $5\text{ cm}$. Subtract both holes from the block.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{block}}&=lwh\\&=14\times9\times5\\&=630\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{one hole}}&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi(2)^{2}\times5\\&=20\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=V_{\text{block}}-2V_{\text{one hole}}\\&=630-2(20\pi)\\&=630-40\pi\\&\approx504.3\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

For one hole, subtract its volume once.

Subtract the inner cylinder from the outer cylinder. Both have length $16\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{outer}}&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi(7)^{2}\times16\\&=784\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{inner}}&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi(5)^{2}\times16\\&=400\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=784\pi-400\pi\\&=384\pi\\&\approx1206.4\text{ cm}^{3}\end{aligned}$

The inside radius is $8\div2=4\text{ m}$. Subtract the inner half-cylinder from the outer half-cylinder.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{outer}}&=\frac12\pi r^{2}h\\&=\frac12\pi(4.5)^{2}\times14\\&=141.75\pi\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{inner}}&=\frac12\pi r^{2}h\\&=\frac12\pi(4)^{2}\times14\\&=112\pi\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=141.75\pi-112\pi\\&=29.75\pi\\&\approx93.462\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A square prism stands on a cylindrical base. The base has diameter $1.6\text{ m}$ and height $0.5\text{ m}$. The square prism has cross-sectional area $0.8\text{ m}^{2}$ and height $6\text{ m}$ above the base. Find the total volume to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
Use the given cross-sectional area directly in $V=Ah$. The cylinder radius is $1.6\div2=0.8\text{ m}$.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{prism}}&=Ah\\&=0.8\times6\\&=4.8\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{base}}&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi(0.8)^{2}\times0.5\\&=0.32\pi\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=4.8+0.32\pi\\&\approx5.8\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

Add the chamber volumes before converting to litres.

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{rectangular}}&=lwh\\&=3\times2\times0.5\\&=3\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{cylindrical}}&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi(0.8)^{2}\times1.5\\&=0.96\pi\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}V&=3+0.96\pi\text{ m}^{3}\end{aligned}$

(a)

$\begin{aligned}C&=1000(3+0.96\pi)\\&\approx6015.9\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

(b) Divide the unrounded capacity by the filling rate.

$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{1000(3+0.96\pi)}{150}\\&\approx40.1\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$
